newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AEA airlines cargo traffic up 3.7 pct in Jan-July.
newsitem.headline: AEA airlines cargo traffic up 3.7 pct in Jan-July.

text.p: Global freight traffic carried by West European airlines in the first seven months of 1996 was up 3.7 percent on the same period last year at 13.29 billion freight tonne-kilometres, FTK, the Association of European Airlines (AEA) said.
The FTK measurement is derived by multiplying the weight of cargo carried by the distance flown.
In January-July 1996, the biggest volume of traffic was transported on Europe-Far East/Australasia routes, the number of FTK flown increasing by 8.2 percent to 4.93 billion FTK.
4.78 billion FTK were flown on Europe-North America air cargo routes, a fall of 1.4 percent on 1995 levels, AEA added.

Europe-Sub-Saharan Africa cargo routes recorded 5.4 percent growth in handling 1.12 billion FTK, while traffic flown on Europe-South Atlantic routes (gateways in Brazil and south of the country) increased by 10.4 percent to 782.1 million FTK.
On Europe-mid-Atlantic routes (gateways south of the U.S. and north of Brazil), cargo traffic transported by Western European airlines totalled 581.5 million FTK, down 4.3 percent.

In the mid and short-haul sector, Europe-Africa/Middle East routes generated 566.1 million FTK, up 15.0 percent on January-July 1995, the highest growth rate achieved by AEA's seven cargo-handling regions.
Intra-European cargo traffic, by contrast, fell by 1.4 percent to 515.8 million FTK.
On global long-haul routes, AEA member airlines flew 12.2 billion FTK, an increase of 3.5 percent on 1995 levels. - Air Cargo Newsroom tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
